Its value is '<hinted> of <decisions> decisions (<pct>%)', where both counts come straight from the session's stored decision records in IndexedDB and pct is exact half-up tenths, computed on its own and not with hintTile. The stored report's hints equal those counts and are its last key. The report is unchanged after reload.

WebKit: 38 decisions, 13 hinted (opened 13); the tile shows '13 of 38 decisions (34.2%)', which matches. Tile order is [report-rate x3, report-hints]; the dd is 18px and does not overflow (scrollWidth = clientWidth). The stored hints equal the independent counts, hints is the last key, and the stored report is byte-identical after reload.

items.evidence: The vitest AC#1 test passes. It asserts report.hints {40,320}, the hintTile value '40 of 320 decisions (12.5%)', the exact tile markup at the end of the 'Volume and errors' dl, and that the rate tiles stay [hands, major, minor]. Holdout: a rendered report with hints puts children in the order [report-rate x3, report-hints], there is exactly one report-hints element, and rateTiles is unchanged by hints -> pass.
The vitest AC#2 test passes and asserts {0,320} and the tile '0 of 320 decisions (0.0%)'. A holdout rounding sweep over h=0 for d=0..400 matches '0.0%' -> pass.

The vitest AC#3 test passes and asserts {25,25}, errors {0,0} with Major grades present, and the tile '25 of 25 decisions (100.0%)'. Holdout: hinted Major/Minor decisions on mixed streets are counted in hints but excluded from errors ({hinted:3, decisions:5}, errors {1,1}) -> pass.

The vitest AC#4 test passes (9.6s). It plays 50 hands in fake-indexeddb, sets hinted by (handNumber+i)%3, and compares the report with the records read back through store.get. It checks 0<hinted<decisions, that getReport equals the returned report, and that the rendered tile value is right. The end-to-end run did the same against real IndexedDB in both browsers -> pass.

The vitest unit test passes. Holdout: hints is the last key, after style/errors/leakCounts. A hand with no decisions anywhere gives {0,0} and the tile '0 of 0 decisions (0.0%)'. One hand without decisions -> hints absent. An old report without hints renders no report-hints element and no 'Hints used' text, and hintTile returns null -> pass.

The vitest unit test passes. Holdout: a sweep over every h<=d for d<=400 plus large and edge pairs (1/2000 -> 0.1%, 1/2001 -> 0.0%, 3/16 -> 18.8%, 1/80 -> 1.3%, 999999/1000000 -> 100.0%) matches exact half-up tenths, with singular 'decision' only when d=1 -> pass.

The vitest unit test passes and covers all 8 specified bad inputs, each checked for its exact RangeError message. Holdout: 5, 'x', {}, decisions '4'/NaN/Infinity/-0.5, missing, 1.5 or null hinted, and hinted 1 with decisions 0 all throw with the correct field. {0,0}, extra properties and a report without hints are accepted -> pass.

The repo e2e report-hints.spec.ts passes in Chromium and WebKit. Its expected tile text comes from hintTile itself (the reviewer's MINOR). To cover that gap, my real-app run computed the expected text separately from the stored records and got matching tiles in both browsers (see end_to_end) -> pass.

findings.expected_vs_actual: The expected tile text in e2e/report-hints.spec.ts comes from the unit under test (hintTile), so a formatting regression in hintTile would not fail that e2e check. The behaviour itself is correct: an independent computation matched in both browsers.
findings.fix: Optional: build the expected value in the e2e from hints.hinted and hints.decisions with its own formatting, or assert a literal value for a known session.
